report.summary: Chunk 5 of 8 of publish.py: render_markdown function builds markdown for council verdict, screen_egress function checks paths and channels for secrets.
risks: screen_egress | medium | The function iterates over channels and paths without early exit optimization on empty inputs; but the code is simple and correct.
render_markdown | low | The function uses _field with many fallback keys; if none exist, it may produce empty strings but no crash.

handoff.purpose: Render council verdict to markdown and screen egress lanes for secrets

symbols.name: render_markdown
symbols.note: Builds a markdown string from verdict, transcript, evidence, council_id. Uses many helper functions defined elsewhere in the file.

symbols.name: screen_egress
symbols.note: Checks paths and channel texts against secret_floor_rule; returns first hit or None.

claims.text: Returns ``(channel, rule)`` for the FIRST hit, or None if clean.
claims.why: The function returns (channel, hit) when hit is truthy, and returns None at the end.

claims.text: The returned rule is a fixed label / path fragment from ``sensitivity`` -- never matched text, so a refusal can be logged and reported without re-leaking the secret it refused (memstore's ``_scan_secret`` posture, same floor, same reason).
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the definition of secret_floor_rule or the _EGRESS_HINT constant, nor does it show the sensitivity module. The claim about the rule being a fixed label cannot be verified here.

claims.text: This comment is a RENDERING. The bus file is the record: it is append-only and hash-chained, so a tampered or truncated transcript is detectable and this comment is not. If the two disagree, the bus is right.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the bus file implementation or the hash-chaining logic. The claim about detectability and precedence cannot be verified here.

claims.text: A turn that did not SPEAK is the quorum honesty story at turn level: bus.py records "refused" / "unavailable" / "budget_exhausted" / "anomaly" rather than dropping the vendor, so rendering the status is the difference between "three vendors agreed" and "one was never asked".
claims.why: The chunk does not include bus.py or its behavior; the claim about bus.py's recording policy cannot be verified.

claims.text: Paths an egress lane declined to send are NAMED, not counted -- a vendor reasoning over less evidence than the others is not an equal voice, and hiding that would make the roster look stronger than it was.
claims.why: The code renders withheld paths as a list of names (via _as_list and _field). The claim about naming rather than counting is consistent with the code.

observations.what: render_markdown uses many helper functions (_field, _text, _short, _turns_of, _bus_path, _chain_head, _as_list) that are defined elsewhere in the file.
screen_egress checks paths first, then channels. It returns the first hit found.
The comment about 'memstore's _scan_secret posture' refers to code outside this chunk.
